Below is a safe, progressive 12‑week conditioning plan tailored for a 58‑year‑old male six months post–myocardial infarction, cleared for Phase II cardiac rehab. It prioritizes aerobic conditioning, low-to-moderate intensity resistance training, mobility, and education. It respects: HR under 70% age‑predicted max (~115 bpm), no Valsalva, no max‑effort lifting, gradual progression, and close monitoring of symptoms. Structure includes three supervised/guided sessions per week plus optional light independent activity. Adjust weekly based on vitals, RPE, recovery, and cardiologist/rehab team input.

Global guardrails and monitoring
- Target intensity:
  - Heart rate: keep under ~115 bpm (70% age‑predicted max). If on beta‑blockers, prefer RPE over HR.
  - RPE: 2–4/10 for early weeks; 3–5/10 by later weeks.
  - Blood pressure: measure pre, during (mid‑aerobic), and post when feasible. Stop if SBP > 180 or DBP > 100, drop of SBP ≥ 10 with symptoms, or symptomatic hypotension.
- Stop exercise immediately and seek medical evaluation if chest pain/pressure, unusual shortness of breath, dizziness, palpitations, radiation of pain to jaw/arm/back, excessive fatigue, or abnormal hemodynamic responses occur.
- Breathing: no Valsalva. Cue diaphragmatic breathing; exhale on exertion, inhale on return.
- Warm‑up/cool‑down: at least 8–10 minutes each, very light intensity.
- Progression: follow the 10% rule for aerobic volume, only one variable at a time (duration before intensity), maintain HR/RPE limits.
- Resistance training: machine or cable dominance for safety and control; avoid overhead straining, isolate tempo; 1–2 seconds up, 2–3 seconds down; stop 2–3 reps before fatigue; no grinding.
- Frequency: 3 structured sessions/week (Mon/Wed/Fri example) + optional low‑intensity walks on non‑session days.

Programme overview by phase
- Phase A (Weeks 1–3): Reintroduction and baseline. Focus on technique, breathing, and establishing tolerable aerobic duration. RPE 2–3.
- Phase B (Weeks 4–6): Build aerobic volume, introduce circuit‑style resistance with light loads. RPE 3–4.
- Phase C (Weeks 7–9): Consolidate endurance, modest progression of resistance volume, add gentle intervals within HR cap. RPE 3–5.
- Phase D (Weeks 10–12): Maintain aerobic volume with variety, refine strength endurance, emphasize independence and home routine. RPE 3–5, HR still <115 bpm.

Session template (most weeks)
1) Pre‑session check (2–3 min): symptoms review, meds taken, BP/HR if available, last session recovery, hydration.
2) Warm‑up (8–10 min): 5–7 min light cardio (treadmill 1–2% incline walk, recumbent bike, or NuStep) + 3 min dynamic mobility (neck rolls, shoulder circles, cat‑camel, hip circles, ankle rocks).
3) Main aerobic (15–35 min depending on week): steady or gentle interval within HR/RPE targets.
4) Resistance circuit (15–25 min): 6–8 exercises, light loads, submax reps, long rests, focus on large muscle groups and postural stability.
5) Cool‑down (8–10 min): 5–7 min very light cardio + 3 min breathing/stretching (calves, quads, hamstrings, chest, back).
6) Post‑session: reassess HR/BP as available; note RPE, any symptoms.

Weeks 1–3: Phase A — Establish base
Goal: comfort with gym routine, consistent 25–35 min total aerobic time/session at low intensity; learn breathing and tempo.

Week 1 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 2 x 8 min steady at RPE 2–3 (HR < 110) with 2–3 min easy between blocks. Modalities: treadmill walk 2–3 mph, recumbent bike light resistance, or NuStep.
- Resistance circuit (1 round, 8–12 reps each, RPE ~3, stop 2–3 reps before fatigue, 60–90 s rest as needed):
  1) Seated leg press (very light)
  2) Seated row (cable/machine, neutral grip)
  3) Chest press machine (light, elbows below shoulder line)
  4) Seated hamstring curl
  5) Cable pulldown to chest (wide‑neutral)
  6) Bodyweight sit‑to‑stand from bench (assisted if needed)
  7) Pallof press (light) or cable anti‑rotation hold
  8) Standing calf raises (bodyweight)
- Mobility: thoracic openers, pec doorway stretch, hip flexor stretch 20–30 s each.

Week 2 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 1 x 12–15 min + 1 x 8–10 min steady, RPE 2–3. Try a second modality within the session (e.g., 12 min treadmill + 8 min bike).
- Resistance: same exercises, 1–2 rounds depending on tolerance. Keep reps 10–12, RPE 3. Add tempo cues; exhale on push/pull, inhale on return.

Week 3 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: Continuous 18–20 min steady, then 5–8 min very light cool‑down cardio within cool‑down block (total aerobic movement ~25–28 min). RPE 2–3.
- Resistance: 2 rounds, 10–12 reps, RPE 3. Introduce light dumbbell options if form solid:
  - DB incline supported row (light) can replace machine row one day.
  - DB floor or machine chest press (very light).
- Balance add‑on: supported tandem stance 2 x 20–30 s.

Weeks 4–6: Phase B — Build volume and strength endurance
Goal: reach 25–30 min continuous aerobic at RPE 3–4; 2 rounds circuit consistently, begin third round selectively.

Week 4
- Aerobic: Continuous 22–25 min steady, HR < 115. Rotate modalities session‑to‑session to reduce joint stress.
- Resistance (2 rounds):
  1) Leg press 12–15 reps
  2) Seated row 12–15
  3) Chest press 10–12
  4) Leg curl 12–15
  5) Lat pulldown 10–12
  6) Supported split squat to bench or step‑back lunge (bodyweight) 8–10/side if tolerated
  7) Cable face pull 12–15 (light)
  8) Pallof press 10–12/side or dead bug 8–10/side (slow)
- Optional finish: 5 min very light cardio flush if HR allows.

Week 5
- Aerobic: 25–28 min steady, RPE 3–4.
- Resistance: 2 rounds most sessions; consider 3rd round on Session 3 if RPE stayed ≤4 and recovery good. Keep same rep ranges; increase load slightly only if HR/RPE remain within targets and technique perfect.

Week 6
- Aerobic: 28–30 min steady, RPE 3–4. One session use an “undulating terrain” treadmill walk (slight 1–3% incline changes) without exceeding HR cap.
- Resistance: 2–3 rounds depending on day. Add:
  - Hip hinge pattern: cable pull‑through or light RDL with dowel/very light DBs 10–12 reps, slow tempo, no breath holding.
  - Farmer carry light kettlebells 2 x 20–30 m with nasal/diaphragmatic breathing (optional; skip if HR spikes).

Weeks 7–9: Phase C — Consolidate, add gentle intervals
Goal: maintain 28–32 min aerobic, introduce mild interval structure staying under HR cap, maintain 2–3 circuit rounds.

Week 7
- Aerobic: 5 min easy + 3 x 5 min “moderate” at upper RPE 4 with 2 min easy between + 5 min easy. Keep HR < 115 throughout; if HR approaches cap, shorten intervals or reduce speed/resistance.
- Resistance (2–3 rounds, 10–12 reps):
  1) Leg press
  2) Seated row
  3) Chest press
  4) Step‑ups to low box 8–10/side (use rails as needed)
  5) Lat pulldown or assisted pull‑down
  6) Cable woodchop low‑to‑high 10/side
  7) Face pull or rear delt fly 12–15
  8) Heel raises 12–15

Week 8
- Aerobic: Continuous 30–32 min steady on a different modality (e.g., elliptical with arms if tolerated, or recumbent bike).
- Resistance: Same as Week 7; progress by adding a third round on one session if RPE allows; do not increase load and rounds in the same week.

Week 9
- Aerobic: Gentle intervals: 6 x 3 min moderate, 2 min easy between, plus 5–8 min easy. RPE peaks 4–5 without HR > 115. If HR tends to overshoot, adjust to 8 x 2 min.
- Resistance: Circuit maintained; consider adding:
  - Single‑arm cable row 10–12/side (anti‑rotation demand).
  - Supported hip airplane or standing hip abduction 10–12/side for lateral hip stability.

Weeks 10–12: Phase D — Maintain, variety, independence skills
Goal: sustain 30–35 min aerobic comfortably, refine strength endurance and daily activity confidence, practice home/independent sessions.

Week 10
- Aerobic: 32–35 min steady; include small cadence variations (e.g., bike rpm changes) staying within HR cap.
- Resistance (2–3 rounds, 10–15 reps):
  1) Leg press
  2) Chest press
  3) Seated or single‑arm row
  4) Leg curl
  5) Step‑ups or split squat
  6) Lat pulldown
  7) Pallof press or cable anti‑rotation walkouts
  8) Core finisher: bird dog 8–10/side (slow, 3‑sec holds)

Week 11
- Aerobic: Choice day: client selects favorite modality. Option A: steady 30–32 min. Option B: 4 x 4 min moderate, 3 min easy between; RPE 4–5 but HR still < 115—scale as needed.
- Resistance: Maintain, adjust exercise variety to keep engagement; keep breathing focus, long rests as needed.

Week 12
- Aerobic: “Graduation” sessions mimic independent routine:
  - Session 1: 30–35 min steady walk outdoors if weather allows, with HR/RPE self‑monitoring.
  - Session 2: Gentle intervals 8 x 2 min moderate/2 min easy on preferred cardio.
  - Session 3: Mixed‑modality 10 min treadmill + 10 min bike + 10 min NuStep, all easy‑moderate.
- Resistance: 2 rounds circuit, emphasize perfect technique and independence cues. Provide a printed/home version with bands for travel days.

Sets, reps, loads guidance
- Start with loads allowing 10–15 reps at RPE 3–4, leaving 2–3 reps in reserve; never strain. If RPE drifts above 4 or HR approaches cap during a set, stop the set.
- Progression lever: first add reps (toward 15), then add a third round on select days, only then consider a small load increase (5–10%) while staying within HR/RPE and symptom‑free.

Weekly structure example
- Monday: Full session (warm‑up, aerobic, resistance, cool‑down)
- Wednesday: Full session
- Friday: Full session
- Optional Tue/Thu/Sat: Leisure walk 20–30 min at RPE 2–3, stretching 10 min.

Flexibility and mobility (each session or on off‑days)
- Lower body: calf stretch, hamstring strap stretch, hip flexor half‑kneeling, glute stretch 20–30 s x 1–2.
- Upper body: pec doorway, thoracic extension over foam roller, lat stretch 20–30 s.
- Breathing: 3–5 min diaphragmatic breathing in crook‑lying or seated at end of session.

Education and lifestyle
- Warm‑up and cool‑down are non‑negotiable for cardiac clients.
- Hydration: sip water before/during/after; avoid large boluses.
- Temperature: avoid strenuous activity in extreme heat/cold; adjust indoor climate as needed.
- Daily activity: encourage 5,000–7,500 steps/day as tolerated, spread through day; avoid prolonged sitting (>45–60 min).
- Medication timing: coordinate sessions around beta‑blockers or nitrates per physician guidance.
- Post‑meal timing: avoid vigorous exercise in the first 60–90 min after large meals.

Nutrition basics for cardiac health (coordinate with RD/physician)
- Emphasize Mediterranean‑style pattern: vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains, nuts, olive oil; fish 2x/week; lean poultry; limit red/processed meats.
- Fiber: target ≥25–30 g/day from whole foods.
- Sodium: aim ~1,500–2,000 mg/day or per MD guidance, especially if hypertension/heart failure history.
- Fats: prioritize mono‑/polyunsaturated, limit saturated, avoid trans fats.
- Portion and weight: gradual weight normalization if indicated (0.25–0.5 kg/week), never via aggressive restriction.
- Alcohol: if consumed, keep within medical advice; often best minimized post‑MI.

Recovery and sleep
- Sleep: 7–9 hours/night; establish consistent schedule.
- Stress: brief daily relaxation (5–10 min breathing, mindfulness, or gentle yoga).
- Soreness: expect mild muscular soreness; avoid DOMS‑inducing protocols. If soreness >48 hours or affects function, reduce next session volume by 20–30%.

Return‑to‑activity and independence by end of Week 12
- Independent plan target: 4–5 days/week aerobic 30–40 min at RPE 3–4, HR under cap; 2 days/week light resistance circuit (8–10 exercises, 1–2 rounds, 10–15 reps).
- Schedule regular check‑ins, monitor BP, lipids, glucose as appropriate, and keep communication with cardiology team.

Notes to you, the trainer
- Individualize daily: if poor sleep/illness/new meds/heat, reduce duration/intensity by 20–30%.
- Maintain symptom diary and RPE log.
- Regressions: swap any lower‑body exercise for seated options on higher‑fatigue days; avoid holds/strains.
- Progress only when all: symptom‑free, HR/BP appropriate, RPE in range, recovery good.

This plan keeps intensity safely below 70% HRmax, avoids Valsalva and max efforts, and builds sustainable conditioning and confidence over 12 weeks. Adjust as needed per medical guidance and client response.

- Gentle mobility after workouts or on off‑days: calf, hamstring, hip flexor, glute, chest, and thoracic mobility, 20–30 s each, 1–2 rounds.
- Balance: supported tandem stance or heel‑to‑toe walks, 2 x 20–30 s.

- Pre‑check: symptoms, meds timing, hydration; take resting HR/BP if available.
- Warm‑up: 8–10 minutes very easy cardio + gentle mobility.
- Main work: steady aerobic (12–25 minutes) and/or light resistance circuit as above.
- Cool‑down: 8–10 minutes very easy cardio + breathing and stretches.
- Monitoring: note peak HR, average RPE, and any symptoms. If HR drifts up or symptoms appear, stop and cool down.

Activities to avoid until re‑cleared
- Intervals, fartlek, tempo/threshold work, hills >2–3%, or rowing if it spikes HR/BP.
- Heavy or near‑failure lifting; high‑strain isometrics; breath holding (Valsalva).
- Power drills (medicine ball slams/throws), loaded carries beyond very light, or long sustained inclines.
- Hot environments, saunas/steam rooms immediately post‑exercise, or outdoor work in high heat/humidity or extreme cold.

Weekly template (example)
- Mon: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + light circuit (6–8 exercises, 1 set each)
- Wed: Steady aerobic 18–22 min + light circuit (1–2 sets each as tolerated)
- Fri: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + mobility/balance
- Tue/Thu/Sat (optional): 10–20 min easy walk + 10 min mobility/breathing

Nutrition, hydration, and timing reminders
- Small, easily digested meal or snack 1.5–2 hours pre‑session; avoid large meals within 60–90 minutes before.
- Sip water before/during/after; follow any fluid/sodium guidance from MD.
- Avoid caffeine or stimulants close to sessions if they elevate HR or provoke symptoms.

Return‑to‑progress criteria (for your notes)
- No chest symptoms across at least 2–3 weeks of sessions.
- Stable HR/BP responses; RPE stays in range; good recovery.
- Cardiology’s explicit clearance to reintroduce intervals or higher‑intensity resistance.

This keeps him conditioned, confident, and safe while minimizing cardiac load until the re‑evaluation. Adjust duration down by 20–30% on poor‑sleep, high‑stress, or hot‑environment days.

Below is a complete, trainer-ready 12-week conditioning program for a 58-year-old male six months post-MI. It includes the original Phase II plan (Weeks 1–7), a Phase III progression (initially planned for Weeks 8–12), and a safety rollback that was enacted after chest tightness during intervals—reverting Weeks 8–12 back to a tightened Phase II until cardiology re-clears progression.

Global guardrails and monitoring (apply throughout)
- Medical status drives intensity. When in Phase II: HR ≤70% age-predicted max (~≤115 bpm unless MD specifies otherwise), RPE 2–4, no Valsalva. When cleared for Phase III: HR ≤85% max (confirm individualized cap), RPE 4–6, brief controlled breath holds allowed at moderate loads only; still no max-effort or grinding.
- Warm-up/cool-down: minimum 8–10 minutes each, very light.
- Stop exercise and seek evaluation if: chest pain/pressure, unusual dyspnea, dizziness/syncope, palpitations, pain radiating to jaw/arm/back, excessive fatigue, abnormal BP/HR responses (SBP > 180 Phase II or >220 Phase III, DBP > 100–110, SBP drop ≥10 mmHg with symptoms).
- Resistance training: machines/cables favored; tempo 2 s up/2–3 s down; leave 2–3 reps in reserve; long rests as needed to manage HR; no isometric straining in Phase II.
- Progression: change one variable at a time; prioritize duration > intensity; follow 10% rule for aerobic volume; only progress if fully symptom-free and vitals appropriate.

Session template (most weeks)
1) Pre-check: symptoms, meds timing, hydration, last-session recovery; take resting HR/BP if available.
2) Warm-up: 5–7 min easy cardio + 3 min gentle mobility.
3) Main aerobic: steady or interval work per phase (Phase III only); Phase II is steady only.
4) Resistance circuit: 6–8 exercises, light to moderate per phase.
5) Cool-down: 5–7 min very light cardio + 3 min breathing/stretching.
6) Post-session: record peak HR, RPE, symptoms.

Weeks 1–3: Phase II — Reintroduction and baseline
Goal: establish routine, technique, and 25–30 min total aerobic movement/session at low intensity.

Week 1 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 2 x 8 min steady at RPE 2–3 (HR well below cap) with 2–3 min easy between.
- Resistance (1 round, 8–12 reps, RPE ~3, 60–90 s rest):
  1) Seated leg press (very light)
  2) Seated cable/machine row (neutral grip)
  3) Chest press machine (light, elbows below shoulder line)
  4) Seated hamstring curl
  5) Lat pulldown to chest (light)
  6) Sit-to-stand from bench
  7) Pallof press (light)
  8) Standing calf raises (bodyweight)
- Mobility: calves, hamstrings, hip flexors, pec doorway, thoracic opener 20–30 s each.

Week 2 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 1 x 12–15 min + 1 x 8–10 min steady, RPE 2–3; try a second modality within the session.
- Resistance: same exercises; 1–2 rounds as tolerated; 10–12 reps, RPE 3; cue breathing.

Week 3 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: Continuous 18–20 min steady + 5–8 min very light cool-down cardio (total movement ~25–28 min).
- Resistance: 2 rounds, 10–12 reps, RPE 3. Optional very light DB row/DB chest press with support if form solid.
- Balance: supported tandem stance 2 x 20–30 s.

Weeks 4–6: Phase II — Build steady endurance and strength endurance
Goal: continuous 25–30 min steady aerobic at RPE 3–4; consistent 2-round circuits, selective third round by Week 6 if HR allows.

Week 4
- Aerobic: Continuous 22–25 min steady; HR ≤115 bpm.
- Resistance (2 rounds):
  1) Leg press 12–15
  2) Seated row 12–15
  3) Chest press 10–12
  4) Leg curl 12–15
  5) Lat pulldown 10–12
  6) Supported split squat or step-back lunge (bodyweight) 8–10/side
  7) Cable face pull 12–15
  8) Pallof press 10–12/side or dead bug 8–10/side (slow)

Week 5
- Aerobic: 25–28 min steady, RPE 3–4.
- Resistance: 2 rounds most sessions; consider a cautious 3rd round on Session 3 only if HR/RPE stable; do not add load and rounds in same week.

Week 6
- Aerobic: 28–30 min steady; one session with small incline undulations (1–3%) if HR remains ≤115.
- Resistance: 2–3 rounds depending on day. Add:
  - Hip hinge: cable pull-through or very light RDL 10–12 reps
  - Optional farmer carry very light 2 x 20–30 m (skip if HR spikes)

Week 7: Phase II — Consolidate before intended transition
Goal: maintain 28–32 min steady; keep resistance quality.

- Aerobic: 28–32 min steady at RPE 3–4; HR ≤115.
- Resistance (2–3 rounds, 10–12 reps):
  1) Leg press
  2) Seated row
  3) Chest press
  4) Step-ups to low box 8–10/side
  5) Lat pulldown
  6) Cable woodchop low-to-high 10/side
  7) Face pull 12–15
  8) Heel raises 12–15

Weeks 8–12: Planned Phase III progression (for reference only; DO NOT USE after chest symptoms)
Note: This block reflects what was initially programmed once Phase III clearance was granted (HR ≤85% max, RPE 4–6, brief controlled breath holds at moderate loads allowed, still no max-effort). After chest tightness during intervals, this block was suspended and replaced by the regression that follows. Keep it on file for future use after explicit medical re-clearance.

Week 8 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Intervals: 6 x 2 min RPE 5 with 2 min easy; plus one 30–32 min steady day and one mixed-modality easy-moderate day.
- Strength: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps (moderate loads) across squat/hinge/push/pull, core, and light carries.

Week 9 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Intervals: 8 x 2 min RPE 5–6 (2 min easy); another day 35 min steady with incline waves 0–3%.
- Strength: progress to 3 sets on key lifts; add unilateral emphasis.

Week 10 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Threshold-style: 3 x 6 min RPE 5–6 (3 min easy) + one long steady 38–40 min.
- Strength: moderate loads 3 x 6–12; light power-skill (very light med-ball passes) pre-lifts.

Week 11 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Fartlek: 30–35 min with 8–10 pickups 45–60 s at RPE 5–6.
- Strength: upper-lower alternation; carries moderate, HR-check after sets.

Week 12 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Benchmark: 10 x 2 min RPE 5–6 (90 s easy) + long steady 40–45 min.
- Strength: finalize take-home routine at moderate loads, 2–3 sets of 8–12.

Weeks 8–12: Active regression back to tightened Phase II (USE THIS after chest tightness until re-cleared)
Global regression rules
- HR: ≤70% max (~≤115 bpm unless stricter MD guidance); RPE 2–3 (max 4 only if fully asymptomatic).
- Aerobic: steady only; remove all intervals; reduce volume initially 25–40% for 7–10 days.
- Resistance: light; 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps; RPE 2–3; leave 3–4 reps in reserve; no Valsalva or straining; 60–120 s rests.
- Monitoring: pre/mid/post HR and BP (if available); symptom log (onset, severity 1–10, duration, relief).

Week 8 (reset/conservative)
- Aerobic: 12–15 min steady + 5–7 min very light cool-down cardio. Modalities: recumbent bike, flat treadmill walk, NuStep.
- Resistance (1 set each, RPE 2–3):
  1) Seated leg press 10–12
  2) Seated row 10–12
  3) Chest press machine 8–10
  4) Seated ham curl 10–12
  5) Lat pulldown 8–10
  6) Sit-to-stand 8–10
  7) Pallof press 8–10/side
  8) Standing calf raise 12–15
- Optional off-day walks: 10–15 min at RPE 2 if symptom-free.

Week 9
- Aerobic: 15–18 min steady; HR ≤115. Stop and cool down if any tightness appears.
- Resistance: 1–2 sets for large patterns only if Week 8 was symptom-free; keep RPE ≤3.
- Balance: supported tandem stance 2 x 20–30 s.

Week 10
- Aerobic: 18–20 min steady; rotate modalities; keep inclines ≤2%.
- Resistance (light): 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps; may add:
  - Cable face pull 12–15 (light)
  - Hip hinge patterning with dowel (no load) 10 slow reps

Week 11
- Aerobic: 20–22 min steady; prioritize diaphragmatic breathing and smooth cadence.
- Resistance: maintain volume; do not add sets and load in same week; stop sets early if HR >110 or RPE drifts upward.
- Core: bird dog 2 x 6–8/side (2–3 s holds).

Week 12
- Aerobic: 22–25 min steady only if Weeks 10–11 fully symptom-free; otherwise hold at last well-tolerated duration.
- Resistance: 1–2 sets, 10–15 reps, RPE 2–3; focus on perfect technique and independence cues.
- Education: reinforce home plan limited to easy walks and light mobility until re-cleared.

Light strength add-ons (optional during regression)
- If a separate light-strength day is desired: 20–25 minutes total; 5–6 exercises; 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps at RPE 2–3; space 24–48 hours apart; reduce or skip if any residual chest symptoms.

Interval conditioning re-introduction (for future, only with explicit clearance)
- Start with 4–6 x 1 min at RPE 4–5 with 2–3 min easy, total work 6–10 min. End any bout that pushes HR above prescribed cap or provokes symptoms. Extend duration before intensity.

Nutrition plan (cardiac-health focused; maintain throughout)
- Pattern: Mediterranean/DASH; plants first; whole grains; legumes; fish 2–3x/week; olive oil primary fat; minimize ultra-processed foods.
- Calories/weight: If weight loss appropriate, aim for a 300–500 kcal/day deficit (~0.25–0.5 kg/week). Otherwise maintain.
- Macros and key targets:
  - Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day from fish, poultry, legumes, low-fat dairy; spread over meals.
  - Fiber: ≥30–40 g/day (10–15 g soluble) from oats, barley, beans, lentils, fruit, flax/chia.
  - Fats: emphasize mono-/polyunsaturated; keep saturated fat <7–10% kcal; avoid trans fats.
  - Sodium: 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless MD directs otherwise; prioritize low-sodium products.
  - Added sugars: <5–10% kcal; limit sugary drinks/desserts.
  - Alcohol: minimize; if permitted, ≤1 drink/day with alcohol-free days; confirm with MD.
- Habits rollout (12 weeks):
  - Weeks 1–2: switch to olive oil; add a veg serving to two meals/day; replace one refined grain with whole grain daily; begin 3–4 day/week food + BP log.
  - Weeks 3–4: add 1 cup beans/lentils ≥4 days/week; include 1 Tbsp ground flax or chia daily; audit sodium and swap to low-/no-salt versions.
  - Weeks 5–6: fish 2–3x/week; ensure 25–35 g protein each meal; add a high-protein snack post-exercise if hungry.
  - Weeks 7–8: replace sweets with fruit + yogurt/nuts most days; eliminate sugar-sweetened beverages.
  - Weeks 9–10: restaurant strategy—grilled/baked entrées, double veggies, sauces on side, request no added salt; keep nuts/fruit on hand when traveling.
  - Weeks 11–12: consolidate 10 “go-to” meals/snacks; maintain 80/20 flexibility; review labs if available.
- Example day (adjust portions to goals):
  - Breakfast: oats with berries, ground flax, walnuts; or veggie omelet + whole-grain toast; or plain Greek yogurt with fruit + chia.
  - Lunch: lentil–quinoa bowl with greens/veg + olive-lemon dressing; or grilled salmon salad with farro; or whole-grain wrap with chicken, hummus, veg.
  - Dinner: baked trout + roasted veg + small baked potato (skin on); or chickpea–veg curry over brown rice; or turkey chili with beans + side salad.
  - Snacks (1–2/day): fruit + nut butter; unsalted nuts; veg + hummus; cottage cheese or yogurt; simple post-workout yogurt + fruit if hungry.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep 7–9 hours nightly; consistent schedule.
- Daily stress management: 5–10 min diaphragmatic breathing or mindfulness.
- Hydration: sip water before/during/after sessions; follow any fluid/sodium restrictions.
- Environment: avoid training in extreme heat/cold; ensure good ventilation.
- Activity on off-days: easy walks and mobility only during regression; after future clearance, resume varied steady work per plan.

Weekly structure (current while regressed)
- Mon: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + light resistance circuit (1 set each)
- Wed: Steady aerobic 18–22 min + light resistance circuit (1–2 sets as tolerated)
- Fri: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + mobility/balance
- Optional Tue/Thu/Sat: 10–20 min easy walk + 10 min mobility/breathing
- Sun: Rest

Return-to-progress criteria (for your notes)
- At least 2–3 weeks without chest symptoms; stable HR/BP responses; RPE in range; good recovery.
- Explicit cardiology clearance specifying new HR cap and any lifting/interval permissions.
- Reintroduce higher intensity gradually: duration first, then gentle intervals, while monitoring symptoms closely.

It includes the original Phase II plan (Weeks 1–7), a Phase III progression (initially planned for Weeks 8–12), and a safety rollback that was enacted after chest tightness during intervals—reverting Weeks 8–12 back to a tightened Phase II until cardiology re-clears progression.

Global guardrails and monitoring (apply throughout)
- Medical status drives intensity. When in Phase II: HR ≤70% age-predicted max (~≤115 bpm unless MD specifies otherwise), RPE 2–4, no Valsalva. When cleared for Phase III: HR ≤85% max (confirm individualized cap), RPE 4–6, brief controlled breath holds allowed at moderate loads only; still no max-effort or grinding.
- Warm-up/cool-down: minimum 8–10 minutes each, very light.
- Stop exercise and seek evaluation if: chest pain/pressure, unusual dyspnea, dizziness/syncope, palpitations, pain radiating to jaw/arm/back, excessive fatigue, abnormal BP/HR responses (SBP > 180 Phase II or >220 Phase III, DBP > 100–110, SBP drop ≥10 mmHg with symptoms).
- Resistance training: machines/cables favored; tempo 2 s up/2–3 s down; leave 2–3 reps in reserve; long rests as needed to manage HR; no isometric straining in Phase II.
- Progression: change one variable at a time; prioritize duration > intensity; follow 10% rule for aerobic volume; only progress if fully symptom-free and vitals appropriate.

Session template (most weeks)
1) Pre-check: symptoms, meds timing, hydration, last-session recovery; take resting HR/BP if available.
2) Warm-up: 5–7 min easy cardio + 3 min gentle mobility.
3) Main aerobic: steady or interval work per phase (Phase III only); Phase II is steady only.
4) Resistance circuit: 6–8 exercises, light to moderate per phase.
5) Cool-down: 5–7 min very light cardio + 3 min breathing/stretching.
6) Post-session: record peak HR, RPE, symptoms.

Weeks 1–3: Phase II — Reintroduction and baseline
Goal: establish routine, technique, and 25–30 min total aerobic movement/session at low intensity.

Week 1 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 2 x 8 min steady at RPE 2–3 (HR well below cap) with 2–3 min easy between.
- Resistance (1 round, 8–12 reps, RPE ~3, 60–90 s rest):
  1) Seated leg press (very light)
  2) Seated cable/machine row (neutral grip)
  3) Chest press machine (light, elbows below shoulder line)
  4) Seated hamstring curl
  5) Lat pulldown to chest (light)
  6) Sit-to-stand from bench
  7) Pallof press (light)
  8) Standing calf raises (bodyweight)
- Mobility: calves, hamstrings, hip flexors, pec doorway, thoracic opener 20–30 s each.

Week 2 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: 1 x 12–15 min + 1 x 8–10 min steady, RPE 2–3; try a second modality within the session.
- Resistance: same exercises; 1–2 rounds as tolerated; 10–12 reps, RPE 3; cue breathing.

Week 3 (3 sessions)
- Aerobic: Continuous 18–20 min steady + 5–8 min very light cool-down cardio (total movement ~25–28 min).
- Resistance: 2 rounds, 10–12 reps, RPE 3. Optional very light DB row/DB chest press with support if form solid.
- Balance: supported tandem stance 2 x 20–30 s.

Weeks 4–6: Phase II — Build steady endurance and strength endurance
Goal: continuous 25–30 min steady aerobic at RPE 3–4; consistent 2-round circuits, selective third round by Week 6 if HR allows.

Week 4
- Aerobic: Continuous 22–25 min steady; HR ≤115 bpm.
- Resistance (2 rounds):
  1) Leg press 12–15
  2) Seated row 12–15
  3) Chest press 10–12
  4) Leg curl 12–15
  5) Lat pulldown 10–12
  6) Supported split squat or step-back lunge (bodyweight) 8–10/side
  7) Cable face pull 12–15
  8) Pallof press 10–12/side or dead bug 8–10/side (slow)

Week 5
- Aerobic: 25–28 min steady, RPE 3–4.
- Resistance: 2 rounds most sessions; consider a cautious 3rd round on Session 3 only if HR/RPE stable; do not add load and rounds in same week.

Week 6
- Aerobic: 28–30 min steady; one session with small incline undulations (1–3%) if HR remains ≤115.
- Resistance: 2–3 rounds depending on day. Add:
  - Hip hinge: cable pull-through or very light RDL 10–12 reps
  - Optional farmer carry very light 2 x 20–30 m (skip if HR spikes)

Week 7: Phase II — Consolidate before intended transition
Goal: maintain 28–32 min steady; keep resistance quality.

- Aerobic: 28–32 min steady at RPE 3–4; HR ≤115.
- Resistance (2–3 rounds, 10–12 reps):
  1) Leg press
  2) Seated row
  3) Chest press
  4) Step-ups to low box 8–10/side
  5) Lat pulldown
  6) Cable woodchop low-to-high 10/side
  7) Face pull 12–15
  8) Heel raises 12–15

Weeks 8–12: Planned Phase III progression (for reference only; DO NOT USE after chest symptoms)
Note: This block reflects what was initially programmed once Phase III clearance was granted (HR ≤85% max, RPE 4–6, brief controlled breath holds at moderate loads allowed, still no max-effort). After chest tightness during intervals, this block was suspended and replaced by the regression that follows. Keep it on file for future use after explicit medical re-clearance.

Week 8 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Intervals: 6 x 2 min RPE 5 with 2 min easy; plus one 30–32 min steady day and one mixed-modality easy-moderate day.
- Strength: 2–3 sets of 8–12 reps (moderate loads) across squat/hinge/push/pull, core, and light carries.

Week 9 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Intervals: 8 x 2 min RPE 5–6 (2 min easy); another day 35 min steady with incline waves 0–3%.
- Strength: progress to 3 sets on key lifts; add unilateral emphasis.

Week 10 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Threshold-style: 3 x 6 min RPE 5–6 (3 min easy) + one long steady 38–40 min.
- Strength: moderate loads 3 x 6–12; light power-skill (very light med-ball passes) pre-lifts.

Week 11 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Fartlek: 30–35 min with 8–10 pickups 45–60 s at RPE 5–6.
- Strength: upper-lower alternation; carries moderate, HR-check after sets.

Week 12 (Phase III plan—shelved)
- Benchmark: 10 x 2 min RPE 5–6 (90 s easy) + long steady 40–45 min.
- Strength: finalize take-home routine at moderate loads, 2–3 sets of 8–12.

Weeks 8–12: Active regression back to tightened Phase II (USE THIS after chest tightness until re-cleared)
Global regression rules
- HR: ≤70% max (~≤115 bpm unless stricter MD guidance); RPE 2–3 (max 4 only if fully asymptomatic).
- Aerobic: steady only; remove all intervals; reduce volume initially 25–40% for 7–10 days.
- Resistance: light; 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps; RPE 2–3; leave 3–4 reps in reserve; no Valsalva or straining; 60–120 s rests.
- Monitoring: pre/mid/post HR and BP (if available); symptom log (onset, severity 1–10, duration, relief).

Week 8 (reset/conservative)
- Aerobic: 12–15 min steady + 5–7 min very light cool-down cardio. Modalities: recumbent bike, flat treadmill walk, NuStep.
- Resistance (1 set each, RPE 2–3):
  1) Seated leg press 10–12
  2) Seated row 10–12
  3) Chest press machine 8–10
  4) Seated ham curl 10–12
  5) Lat pulldown 8–10
  6) Sit-to-stand 8–10
  7) Pallof press 8–10/side
  8) Standing calf raise 12–15
- Optional off-day walks: 10–15 min at RPE 2 if symptom-free.

Week 9
- Aerobic: 15–18 min steady; HR ≤115. Stop and cool down if any tightness appears.
- Resistance: 1–2 sets for large patterns only if Week 8 was symptom-free; keep RPE ≤3.
- Balance: supported tandem stance 2 x 20–30 s.

Week 10
- Aerobic: 18–20 min steady; rotate modalities; keep inclines ≤2%.
- Resistance (light): 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps; may add:
  - Cable face pull 12–15 (light)
  - Hip hinge patterning with dowel (no load) 10 slow reps

Week 11
- Aerobic: 20–22 min steady; prioritize diaphragmatic breathing and smooth cadence.
- Resistance: maintain volume; do not add sets and load in same week; stop sets early if HR >110 or RPE drifts upward.
- Core: bird dog 2 x 6–8/side (2–3 s holds).

Week 12
- Aerobic: 22–25 min steady only if Weeks 10–11 fully symptom-free; otherwise hold at last well-tolerated duration.
- Resistance: 1–2 sets, 10–15 reps, RPE 2–3; focus on perfect technique and independence cues.
- Education: reinforce home plan limited to easy walks and light mobility until re-cleared.

Light strength add-ons (optional during regression)
- If a separate light-strength day is desired: 20–25 minutes total; 5–6 exercises; 1–2 sets of 10–15 reps at RPE 2–3; space 24–48 hours apart; reduce or skip if any residual chest symptoms.

Interval conditioning re-introduction (for future, only with explicit clearance)
- Start with 4–6 x 1 min at RPE 4–5 with 2–3 min easy, total work 6–10 min. End any bout that pushes HR above prescribed cap or provokes symptoms. Extend duration before intensity.

Nutrition plan (cardiac-health focused; maintain throughout)
- Pattern: Mediterranean/DASH; plants first; whole grains; legumes; fish 2–3x/week; olive oil primary fat; minimize ultra-processed foods.
- Calories/weight: If weight loss appropriate, aim for a 300–500 kcal/day deficit (~0.25–0.5 kg/week). Otherwise maintain.
- Macros and key targets:
  - Protein: ~1.0–1.2 g/kg/day from fish, poultry, legumes, low-fat dairy; spread over meals.
  - Fiber: ≥30–40 g/day (10–15 g soluble) from oats, barley, beans, lentils, fruit, flax/chia.
  - Fats: emphasize mono-/polyunsaturated; keep saturated fat <7–10% kcal; avoid trans fats.
  - Sodium: 1,500–2,000 mg/day unless MD directs otherwise; prioritize low-sodium products.
  - Added sugars: <5–10% kcal; limit sugary drinks/desserts.
  - Alcohol: minimize; if permitted, ≤1 drink/day with alcohol-free days; confirm with MD.
- Habits rollout (12 weeks):
  - Weeks 1–2: switch to olive oil; add a veg serving to two meals/day; replace one refined grain with whole grain daily; begin 3–4 day/week food + BP log.
  - Weeks 3–4: add 1 cup beans/lentils ≥4 days/week; include 1 Tbsp ground flax or chia daily; audit sodium and swap to low-/no-salt versions.
  - Weeks 5–6: fish 2–3x/week; ensure 25–35 g protein each meal; add a high-protein snack post-exercise if hungry.
  - Weeks 7–8: replace sweets with fruit + yogurt/nuts most days; eliminate sugar-sweetened beverages.
  - Weeks 9–10: restaurant strategy—grilled/baked entrées, double veggies, sauces on side, request no added salt; keep nuts/fruit on hand when traveling.
  - Weeks 11–12: consolidate 10 “go-to” meals/snacks; maintain 80/20 flexibility; review labs if available.
- Example day (adjust portions to goals):
  - Breakfast: oats with berries, ground flax, walnuts; or veggie omelet + whole-grain toast; or plain Greek yogurt with fruit + chia.
  - Lunch: lentil–quinoa bowl with greens/veg + olive-lemon dressing; or grilled salmon salad with farro; or whole-grain wrap with chicken, hummus, veg.
  - Dinner: baked trout + roasted veg + small baked potato (skin on); or chickpea–veg curry over brown rice; or turkey chili with beans + side salad.
  - Snacks (1–2/day): fruit + nut butter; unsalted nuts; veg + hummus; cottage cheese or yogurt; simple post-workout yogurt + fruit if hungry.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep 7–9 hours nightly; consistent schedule.
- Daily stress management: 5–10 min diaphragmatic breathing or mindfulness.
- Hydration: sip water before/during/after sessions; follow any fluid/sodium restrictions.
- Environment: avoid training in extreme heat/cold; ensure good ventilation.
- Activity on off-days: easy walks and mobility only during regression; after future clearance, resume varied steady work per plan.

Weekly structure (current while regressed)
- Mon: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + light resistance circuit (1 set each)
- Wed: Steady aerobic 18–22 min + light resistance circuit (1–2 sets as tolerated)
- Fri: Steady aerobic 15–20 min + mobility/balance
- Optional Tue/Thu/Sat: 10–20 min easy walk + 10 min mobility/breathing
- Sun: Rest

Return-to-progress criteria (for your notes)
- At least 2–3 weeks without chest symptoms; stable HR/BP responses; RPE in range; good recovery.
- Explicit cardiology clearance specifying new HR cap and any lifting/interval permissions.
- Reintroduce higher intensity gradually: duration first, then gentle intervals, while monitoring symptoms closely.

This single document gives you the full 12-week flow, the originally planned Phase III block (now on hold), and the enacted Phase II regression for Weeks 8–12 to prioritize safety after symptoms. Adjust any element day to day based on vitals, symptoms, sleep, meds, and physician guidance.
